claims.text: A thin VFeTiTaW high-entropy-alloy interlayer at the W–Cu interface will increase the composite's overall thermal conductivity.
The VFeTiTaW interlayer will preserve the W–Cu composite's mechanical integrity.
The VFeTiTaW interlayer will preserve the W–Cu composite's irradiation resistance.
A conformal, thin VFeTiTaW interlayer can be introduced between the tungsten and copper phases during fabrication.
The intervention is applicable under high-thermal-flux conditions relevant to fusion reactors.
The intervention is applicable at elevated temperatures and under particle irradiation.
The high-entropy interlayer improves bonding at the W–Cu interface.
The interlayer reduces interfacial thermal resistance.
The interlayer minimizes stress concentrations at the W–Cu interface.
The interlayer acts as a barrier to irradiation-induced defect accumulation.
The composition and microstructure of VFeTiTaW improve phonon coupling across tungsten and copper.
The composition and microstructure of VFeTiTaW improve electron coupling across tungsten and copper.
The interlayer provides a more efficient heat-transfer pathway without introducing mechanically weak interfaces.
VFeTiTaW has demonstrated irradiation resistance that will help maintain structural and performance stability under neutron or ion bombardment.
The interlayered composite will retain mechanical durability comparable to a W–Cu composite without the interlayer.
The interlayered composite will retain irradiation resistance comparable to a W–Cu composite without the interlayer.
The interlayer must be sufficiently thin to avoid becoming a thermal barrier.
Long-term microstructural stability of the VFeTiTaW interlayer under thermal and irradiation exposure remains uncertain and requires validation.
